issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. 'lecture_name', 'number_of_inscribed_students') but the rest of the class (constructor, getters/setters, methods) uses camelCase field names (e.g. 'lectureName', 'numberOfInscribedStudents'). This name mismatch means the declared fields are never used and the references to camelCase fields are to undeclared variables, causing compilation failure and contradicting the UML/ specification which uses camelCase names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent with the UML and the rest of the class. Rename the declared fields to camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) or update all usages to the declared snake_case names. Ensure the constructor and all methods assign to and reference the same field names so the class compiles and matches the specification.

issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case identifiers (e.g., lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) while the problem statement (UML) and the rest of the solution code (constructor, getters/setters, methods) use camelCase names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This mismatch creates a semantic and technical inconsistency: students expect the attributes named as in the UML/camelCase and the solution's methods reference those camelCase names, but the declared field identifiers differ, causing confusion and compilation errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Use consistent camelCase attribute names that match the UML and the rest of the class. Rename the declared fields in Lecture.java to: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; or alternatively adjust all usages to the declared snake_case names — the recommended fix is to align declarations to camelCase to match the problem statement and method implementations.
